headline: The run-to-run variance that agent benchmarks report at temperature 0 is the serving stack's batch-dependent arithmetic, not the agent, and over multi-turn trajectories it is large enough to reorder leaderboards.
raised_by: Jacob, 2026-10-20 03:13 ET, in chat: Thinking Machines' post on defeating nondeterminism in LLM inference is adjacent to our luck-subtraction thread
current_belief: Fetched 2026-10-20 from thinkingmachines.ai/blog/defeating-nondeterminism-in-llm-inference (Horace He and Thinking Machines Lab, 2025-09-10): the forward pass is run-to-run deterministic, but kernels whose reduction order changes with batch size make a request's numerics depend on the other requests in the batch, so 'from each user's perspective the output is nondeterministic'; Qwen3-235B-A22B at temperature 0, 1000 completions of 1000 tokens: 80 unique completions, identical for the first 102 tokens; with batch-invariant kernels all 1000 identical; cost on Qwen3-8B, 1000 sequences: 26 s default vs 55 s unoptimised vs 42 s with the improved attention kernel (about 2.1x and 1.6x). The post frames this as reproducibility and on-policy RL (sampler-trainer KL flat at 0) and does not discuss benchmark evaluation. The field's working belief to test at the kill search: temperature-0 agent evaluations are reported as single runs or with a 'noise' of a point or two, as if deterministic.
if_true: Every temperature-0 benchmark report states its serving stack and whether decoding was batch-invariant; leaderboards add a stack-noise column or run batch-invariant; and the per-turn luck-skill decomposition (W41 product red team C, parked) becomes exactly identifiable on the agent side: a batch-invariant agent at temperature 0 has zero decision variance by construction, so Var[R] decomposes onto the user simulator and environment alone - the control arm that instrument lacked.
if_false: At trajectory scale the token-level divergences rarely change an action's outcome (flip rate under 2 percent, rank order stable) - a reassuring measurement benchmark owners would still cite when they report temperature-0 numbers; the luck-skill thread stays parked on its consumer verdict.
relates_to: W41 product red team C: per-turn luck/skill attribution for user-simulator benchmarks (parked in L1; data/reports/2026-W41-product-redteam-C.md) - this claim supplies the exact zero-variance agent arm that the split needed
standards.md Gate 0: 'a party at temperature 0 has zero decision variance by construction' now holds only with batch-invariant decoding; without it, temperature 0 is a protocol artifact
probes: P-W43-J01-a (thought; 15-25 GPU-h, $50-80, 4 days): outcome-flip rate at temperature 0, default stack vs batch-invariant, on a multi-turn agent benchmark with open models

P-W43-J01-a.what: Outcome-flip rate at temperature 0: default serving stack (batch composition varied by concurrency) versus batch-invariant decoding, agent and user simulator both an 8B open model at temperature 0, on a multi-turn benchmark with deterministic tools
P-W43-J01-a.design: Two arms x 10 repeats x 100 tasks. Default arm: vLLM default kernels, each repeat run at a different concurrency (alone, 8, 32) so batch composition changes. Treatment arm: the same stack with batch-invariant kernels (TML's released kernels or vLLM's batch-invariant mode - which exists and works for the model is checked at the kill search); its flip rate must be exactly 0, which is the determinism check. Record per task: any outcome disagreement across the 10 repeats, the turn of first divergence, pass^k for k=1..10, and the rank order of three agent variants (prompt or scaffold variants) per repeat.
P-W43-J01-a.kill_probe: Dead if the default arm's outcome-flip rate is under 2 percent of tasks AND the rank order of the three agent variants is identical across all ten repeats. Expected (judgment): 5-15 percent flips on 30-turn tasks and at least one adjacent-rank swap. Field's assumption: temperature 0 is deterministic or noise of a point. Belief-changing: over 15 percent or a non-adjacent rank reversal. 15-25 GPU-hours on one H100, $50-80, 4 days.
neighbors_to_check_first: the TML post and the kernels it released (2025-09-10)
vLLM and SGLang deterministic or batch-invariant inference modes (dates and coverage)
any paper measuring temperature-0 output nondeterminism of LLMs or agents across runs (search: nondeterminism, 'temperature 0', reproducibility, batch, variance, agent benchmark)
benchmark reports that run agents at temperature 0 and how they report variance (tau-bench, SWE-bench, terminal-bench - read their own text)

scorecard.target_value: Asked in print: the TML post (fetched) calls reproducibility 'a bedrock of scientific progress' and shows 80 unique completions in 1000 at temperature 0, but stops before evaluation - that is the gap. Who pays: benchmark owners who report temperature-0 numbers, and anyone ranking agents a few points apart. Missing: a benchmark owner's own statement about temperature-0 variance - kill search.

impact_ceiling.floor: A measured flip-rate and first-divergence-turn table for one benchmark and one model; a note people cite when they report temperature-0 numbers. Requires the probe. p = 0.7 (judgment).
impact_ceiling.middle: The number is large enough that benchmark owners add a serving-stack column or adopt batch-invariant decoding for official runs. Requires flips over 5 percent or a rank swap. p = 0.25 (judgment).
impact_ceiling.ceiling: The exact zero-variance agent arm re-opens the parked per-turn luck-skill instrument with a clean identification, and the pair becomes a standards paper on deterministic evaluation of agents. Requires the middle result plus the parked item's consumer objection answered. p = 0.1 (judgment).

scorecard.relevance: L1 (reliability, variance attribution): direct. L3 and the systems route (Lloyd, Netravali, Dao): batch-invariant kernels are their vocabulary; direct. Narasimhan route via tau-bench as the natural testbed. Industry: every eval team. Jacob's edge: GPU numerics and kernels (computer engineering) load-bearing. Zero for L5 and for any robotics consumer.
scorecard.kill_probe: P-W43-J01-a above: 15-25 GPU-h, $50-80, 4 days; dead if flips under 2 percent and ranks identical across ten repeats.
scorecard.density_and_ownership: Unknown until the kill search (12-month arXiv API count with mechanism words - batch invariance, reduction order, nondeterminism - AND role words - benchmark, evaluation, agent, pass^k; two pre-window precedents; the two closest papers' limitation text). Incumbents to check: TML's kernels, vLLM/SGLang deterministic modes, any 'temperature 0 is not deterministic' measurement.
scorecard.why_now: Batch-invariant kernels (2025-09-10) make a truly zero-variance agent arm available for the first time; before them, stack noise and agent decision variance at temperature 0 could not be separated, so nobody could measure the first in isolation.
scorecard.register: Measurement (a ruler for serving-stack noise at benchmark scale) with a standards consequence (what a temperature-0 report must state). It is not a new kernel, not a benchmark, not a method, and not a claim about sampling at temperature above 0.

P-W43-01-2x2.what: The simulator-budget 2x2: train a policy at the shipped solver budget (Go1 iterations=1; Leap iterations=5) and at the converged budget (iterations=100, tol 1e-8) under the full training protocol (DR, kicks, observation noise, sampled actions) with a wall-clock-matched arm; evaluate every policy in both engines with paired DR draws and seeds; the interaction term J_conv(pi_conv) - J_conv(pi_cap) - [J_cap(pi_conv) - J_cap(pi_cap)] is the cap-isolated exploit; the certificate ||g_K|| and nchange logged per step are the fidelity column; sim2sim across engines (Playground's shipped script) is the field-standard transfer proxy; hardware is the ceiling arm.
P-W43-01-2x2.kill_probe: Dead if the interaction term lies inside the batch-seed interval of zero on BOTH Go1 rough terrain and the Leap cube task. Pre-registered (judgment): Go1 interaction about zero (sticking contacts; the hardware prior), Leap interaction positive and a non-trivial share of return (many simultaneous contacts; SAPU's interpenetration exploit in assembly is the precedent). Field's assumption: DR absorbs numerical error everywhere, and Leap failures are hardware flex and geometry. Belief-changing: a positive Leap interaction that shrinks with budget at matched wall-clock. Cost: two retrains per task at minutes each on 2 GPUs, cross-evaluation in minutes; 4-10 GPU-hours including the Leap retrain (no public Leap checkpoint), $20-50, one week.

headline: A GPU simulator's physics budget is a dose: transferable policy return follows one dose-response curve in solver budget per task class, so fidelity can be scheduled during training like a learning rate instead of fixed by a config file.
raised_by: Jacob and the operator, 2026-10-21 discuss session on the simulator thread (the systems half of L5, now framed as the consequence of a measurement)
current_belief: Solver budgets are fixed per task in model files (Playground XML iterations=1 Go1, 5 Leap; legged_gym num_position_iterations=4) and justified by DR (MJX docs, fetched 2026-10-20 in the C-W43-15 red team); numerical settings are treated as a randomization axis (Dactyl randomized the time step), not a dial; the only fetched RL consumer of a fidelity scalar is a control-variate estimator (MFPG-PPO 2610.02505).
if_true: Training recipes gain a fidelity schedule (coarse early, converged late) at matched wall-clock; engine teams expose the budget per world as a runtime knob rather than a file constant; the iteration-level scheduler (the lane's systems piece) has a stated consumer.
if_false: Response is task-specific or non-monotone: fixed budgets are right and the scheduler has no consumer - a result engine teams would still cite when choosing defaults.
probes: P-W43-01-2x2 (rides on CL-W43-01's probe: the dose-response of transferable return in budget comes free from the 2x2 plus two intermediate budgets)
C-W43-16 (compute-matched fidelity mixture vs fixed cap in GPU RL; 50 GPU-h, $150, 7 d) - the recipe test
